-37.10711,144.06074: Mechanics' Institute. Beginning as early as 1855 in October 1866 the Newstead Debating and Reading Club officially became the Newstead Mechanics' Institute and, as you see on the facade, the building followed in 1868. To the right is Colquhoun's Store, built in 1868 and to the left, Rowe's Boot Shop, built in 1878. In the mid-1920s, Cusack's Motors was established on the land between the Book Shop and the Mechanics' Institute. Note the gas lamp and the sign on Mechanics' Institute announcing 'Skating every Saturday...'.
-37.10711,144.06075: Shire of Newstead. The underside of this plaque records the peak level of the flood which took place on the 19th August 1909.
-37.13749,144.34739: Taradale Mechanics' Institute. Established on this site c. 1858. The Mechanics' Institute movement began in British urban industrial centres in the early 1800s. A "mechanic" was a person applying skills and technology. During the 19th century, most towns in Victoria established a Mechanics' Institute or Athenaeum with a library and meeting hall. Common objects were the "spread of useful knowledge" and provision for "rational recreation" in the community. This plaque, No. 4 in the MIV series, was unveiled in 2004.
-37.18877,144.38454: Caroline Chisholm Shelter Sheds 1855. The Mechanics Institute and antique shop now occupy the area upon which the Malmsbury shelter sheds stood. 10 such sheds from Essendon to Elphinstone a days walk apart accomodated single persons and married couples at fixed low prices.

Malmsbury Mechanics' Institute. Founded 1862. First met on this site 1862. The Mechanics' Institute movement began in British urban industrial centres in the early 1800s. A "mechanic" was a person applying skills and technology. During the 19th century, most towns in Victoria established a Mechanics' Institute or Athenaeum with a library and meeting hall. Common objects were the "spread of useful knowledge" and provision for "rational recreation" in the community.The Malmsbury Mechanics’ Institute (MMI) was formed in 1862. The former Caroline Chisholm Shelter Shed, on this site, was renovated for use as council chambers by the Borough of Malmsbury in 1862, and space was granted to the MMI. The site was purchased by the Institute in 1871. The two front rooms of the present building were built in 1876, the Fedral Hall at the rear in 1895. This plaque, No. 27 in the MIV series, was placed here in 2012 by Malmsbury Historical Society to mark the 150th anniversary of the establishment of MMI.
-37.2368,144.33893: Drummond Public Hall. In the 1920s the hall was relocated by Councillor William Main to its present site from Lauriston where it had been used for dances and entertainment for the war effort (World War 1) and as a courtroom. In 1922 the hall was used as a Free Library and for community activities such as square dancing.
-37.24728,144.45347: Kyneton Shire Hall. Local Government, one of the States earliest, dates from 1856. The southern bays of the present facade were built in 1877-78. The building with combined town hall / picture theatre was completed in 1929.
-37.2481,144.4539: Kyneton Savings Bank. A savings bank opened in Piper Street in 1861, moved here in 1884, became a branch of the State Savings Bank, then merged with the Commonwealth Bank in 1991. The building is brick with a rendered facing. Notable features are the windows and entrance with classical details and the balustraded parapet above. The design by architects Caselli & Figgis was later used at Maryborough and Warrnambool.
-37.24954,144.45318: Kyneton Mechanics' Institute. Opened 19 October 1858. The Mechanics' Institute movement began in British urban industrial centres in the early 1800s. A "mechanic" was a person applying skills and technology. During the 19th century, most towns in Victoria established a Mechanics' Institute or Athenaeum with a library and meeting hall. Common objects were the "spread of useful knowledge" and provision for "rational recreation" in the community. In 1855 a committee was formed to establish the Kyneton Mechanics' Institute. The first building opened in 1858, had meeting rooms and a library. Serious fires in 1867 and 1876 destroyed large sections of the building and its valuable library. In 1897 fire damaged the room of the main hall. The building was rebuilt after each of these fires. The original hall had a mural in a Grecian theme that was later replaced with an Art Deco design. The restoration and refurbishment in recent years has returned a grand building to the community where people can meet and socialise in the heart of the town. This plaque, No. 49 in the MIV series, was placed here in 2015. It is dedicated to the pioneers who established the reserve and built the hall.
-37.41996,144.11635: Leonards Hill Public Hall. The former Mechanics Institute and Free Library was constructed in 1884 in the small timber milling settlement of Leonard's Hill. The township was established to supply hewn and split timber from the Wombat Forests to the gold mining companies around the district.
-37.47473,144.03686: Mollongghip Hall. The hall was built by local labour in the late 19th century. It has been the social centre for the farming community for over 100 years.
